items.title: Global food prices jump for second straight month as Middle East war disrupts supply chains

featured_image.name: Consumer prices rose 2.4% annually in February, as expected - CNBC

items.description:
Global food commodity prices rose for a second consecutive month in March, climbing 2.4 percent as the escalating conflict in the Middle East sent energy and fertilizer costs surging through agricultural supply chains, according to data released Friday by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations.

The FAO Food Price Index, which tracks monthly changes in a basket of internationally traded food commodities, averaged 128.5 points in March, up from a revised 125.5 in February. The increase marks the sharpest monthly jump in the index since mid-2025 and follows February's 0.9 percent rise, which had ended a five-month streak of declines.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: South Korea, France elevate ties to strategic partnership

featured_image.name: Macron visits Japan and South Korea, both worried about war in Iran

items.description:
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung and French President Emmanuel Macron elevated their countries' relationship to a "global strategic partnership" on Friday following summit talks in Seoul, marking the most notable overhaul of bilateral ties in more than two decades.[1][2]

The upgrade replaces a "comprehensive partnership for the 21st century" that had been in place since 2004. It comes as the two nations celebrate the 140th anniversary of diplomatic relations and seek closer alignment on defense, energy security, and advanced technology amid what French officials described as "significant international and regional tensions".[2][3][1]

items.title: Half of Iran's missile launchers intact after weeks of strikes, assessment finds

featured_image.name: US says it has destroyed Iran missile capacity - Al Jazeera

items.description:
A new U.S. intelligence assessment indicates that roughly half of Iran's missile launchers remain intact and thousands of one-way attack drones are still in its arsenal after five weeks of intensive American and Israeli airstrikes, according to CNN. The findings directly undercut repeated claims by President Trump and senior officials that Iran's military capabilities have been all but eliminated since Operation Epic Fury began on February 28.[1]

In a national address on April 1, Trump told Americans that Iran's "missiles are just about used up or beaten," adding that "their navy is gone, their air force is gone". Earlier, on his Truth Social account, Trump declared that "Iran has been, essentially, decimated". Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has cited a 90 percent drop in Iranian missile launches since the start of the conflict.[2][3]

items.title: US denies Iran's claim it downed warplane near Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: US Air Force conducts airstrikes with F-35 for first time ever

items.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps on Thursday claimed it intercepted and destroyed an advanced warplane belonging to the United States and Israel south of Qeshm Island in the Persian Gulf, according to a statement carried by Iranian media. The IRGC said the aircraft crashed into Gulf waters after being struck by its air defense systems, though no details were provided about the type of aircraft or its crew. Iranian state television broadcast footage it said showed the moment the warplane was hit.[1]

US Central Command swiftly rejected the claim. "All U.S. fighter aircraft are accounted for. Iran's IRGC has made the same false claim at least half a dozen times," CENTCOM said in a post on X.[2][3]

items.title: SpaceX in talks with Saudi fund for $5B anchor stake in record IPO

featured_image.name: SpaceX filed confidential SEC IPO papers, eyes $1.75 ...

items.description:
SpaceX has held discussions with Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund about a roughly $5 billion anchor investment in what is shaping up to be the largest initial public offering in history, Reuters reported on Wednesday. The talks come just one day after the rocket and satellite company confidentially filed its IPO registration with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, according to Bloomberg.[1][2][3]

The investment would partly prevent dilution of PIF's existing stake of just under 1% in SpaceX, according to people familiar with the matter. No final decision has been made, and any investment remains subject to change, the sources cautioned.[4][2][1]

items.title: IRGC launches fresh strikes on steel, aluminum plants across Middle East

featured_image.name: Iranian attacks across Gulf continue as major industrial ...

items.description:
Iranian missile and drone strikes have knocked two of the Middle East's largest aluminum smelters offline, pushing prices on the London Metal Exchange to levels not seen since 2022 and raising fears of a prolonged global supply crisis.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed responsibility for weekend strikes on March 28 that hit Emirates Global Aluminium's Al Taweelah plant in Abu Dhabi and Aluminium Bahrain's main facility. EGA reported "substantial damage" and injuries to six employees, while Alba said two workers were hurt as it assessed the impact on operations. On April 2, the IRGC announced a fresh "90th wave" of Operation True Promise 4, striking additional steel and aluminum facilities across the region tied to U.S. interests.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Bahrain pushes for Friday UN vote to authorize force in Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Bahrain pushes UN-backed action for Hormuz shipping

items.description:
Bahrain's Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani on Thursday urged the United Nations Security Council to take a "decisive response" to Iran's effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, calling for a vote on a Bahraini draft resolution as early as Friday that would authorize "all necessary means" to protect commercial shipping through the critical waterway.[1][2]

Speaking during a high-level Council session that Bahrain chaired as part of its April presidency, Al Zayani condemned Iran's "unlawful and unjustified attempt to control international navigation in the Strait of Hormuz," warning that Tehran's actions threaten energy security, food supplies, and global trade. He also denounced Iranian ballistic missile and drone strikes on Gulf states targeting civilian infrastructure, including airports, water facilities, seaports, and hotels.[3][2][1]
